title: Inline comment signal map — personal review heuristics
content:
Objective:
- Capture lightweight heuristics for interpreting inline review comments quickly (what needs immediate action vs. follow-up vs. FYI).
- Produce a small, reproducible signal map I can use while triaging a review queue and to seed a bot later.

Context / why this matters:
- I spend ~20–30% of review time deciding whether a comment is blocking, optional, or noisy.
- Small contractors + rotating on-call reviewers contribute inconsistent phrasing; having a heuristic speeds the triage loop and reduces ping fatigue.

Signal categories (ranked for triage):
1) BLOCKER (must fix before merge) — immediate action
   - Keywords: "regression", "breaks", "security", "wrong result", "data loss", "racy", "undefined behavior"
   - Examples: "This change causes request timeouts", "Will break existing saved workflows"
   - Signals: references to a test, CI failure, or specific user-visible bug id improve confidence
   - Action: mark PR as blocked, add reviewer assignment, require fix commit or explicit waiver from owner

2) CORRECTNESS / LOGIC — high priority but may be fix-in-place or follow-up depending on scope
   - Keywords: "off-by-one", "edge case", "null handling", "tokenization mismatch"
   - Examples: "What happens if model output is empty?", "This math is inverted for negative scores"
   - Action: ask for a small repro or unit test; if trivial, request patch; if deep, request an issue + label "follow-up: correctness"

3) SECURITY / PRIVACY — treated as BLOCKER for private deployments
   - Keywords: "secrets", "plaintext", "k-anon", "PII", "leak"
   - Examples: "Exposes S3 key in logs", "serializes user PII to metrics"
   - Action: immediate stop and escalate to security team for Private deployments; put hold on merge until sign-off

4) STYLE / CONSISTENCY — low priority, often optional
   - Keywords: "nit", "style", "nit:", "format"
   - Examples: "nit: rename this var", "nit: use fold-left"
   - Action: optional small follow-up commit; prefer to batch these into a cleanup PR unless they reduce clarity

5) PERFORMANCE / COST — medium priority depending on SLOs
   - Keywords: "hot loop", "allocations", "hotpath", "cache miss", "batching"
   - Examples: "This allocs per token", "I think we can use KV cache here"
   - Action: if storage/latency/cost impact likely > 5% or in a hotpath, treat as high and require benchmarks or canary; otherwise tag "perf: investigate"

6) USABILITY / DOCS / API contract — actionable but often post-merge
   - Keywords: "docs", "signature", "error message", "API"
   - Examples: "error message not actionable for integrators"
   - Action: create issue for docs updates; if the change affects user-visible contract, require patch before merge
n
Heuristic scoring (quick mental model):
- +3 severity: blocker/security with CI/test evidence
- +2 severity: correctness, performance with evidence/benchmark
- +1 severity: usability/docs increases cognitive load or ambiguous error strings
- -1 severity: nit/style
- If score >= 3 -> block/require; 1–2 -> require explicit owner comment/plan; <=0 -> optional

Quick checklist when I open a PR:
- Read title + description: does it include a user story or bug id?
- Scan CI: failing tests -> immediate stop
- Search for inline "TODO" or "XXX" in changed files
- Grep for secrets/keys (small script below)
- Prioritize comments using signal categories above

Small scripts / tools I use (notes to self):
- secret grep: (simple) grep -E "(AKIA|AIza|-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY|ssh-rsa)" -n || add heuristics for base64-like blobs
- quick perf check: run a microbenchmark of changed function vs main branch using `pytest -k perf --bench` (we need to standardize this)
- comment classifier prototype: `review-signal.py --pr 4217` (local prototype that uses keyword weights above)

Patterns I see & suggested team conventions:
- "nit:" prefix is 80% harmless; prefer reviewers use the prefix so bots can auto-classify
- Always include an expected outcome in a correctness comment (e.g., "I expect X to be non-null because Y"); fewer follow-ups if comment asks for a repro
- For private deployments, tag security-related comments with "security:" explicitly
- Use labels on PRs: perf/will-change-user-experience/docs/blocker to make triage visible

Automation ideas (MVP):
- Small bot that tags comments by keyword weight and posts a summary comment: "Signals: 1 blocker, 2 correctness, 3 nit"
- Auto-add checklist when PR description contains "WIP"/"RFC" to prevent accidental merge
- Suggest checklist template: Regression test? Bench results? Docs? Changelog?

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (note to follow up):
- How conservative should the bot be? (Blocking false positives are costly; missing regressions are costly too)
- Do we allow style nits to be auto-fixed via CI (prettier/gofmt) or do we insist on human commit?
- For performance comments without a benchmark, do we require a microbenchmark before blocking? Who writes it?

Concrete follow-ups for me:
- 2024-10-20: prototype `review-signal.py` for PR 4217 and 4339; log false positives
- 2024-10-25: propose a labels template in #eng-reviews Slack thread and add a sample PR description template (assign to Maya)
- 2024-11-05: run a survey of 6 reviewers asking common phrasing they use for blocking vs optional comments (quick 5 min form)

Example quick note snippets for copy/paste to PR: 
- "Blocker: please add a regression test or explain why this can't be tested. Marking as blocked until addressed."
- "Nit: rename var x -> readable_name. optional, push lumped cleanup later."
- "Perf: this increments allocations on hotpath, can we benchmark? If >5% increase we should avoid this approach."

Mini retrospective after trying this on a few reviews:
- Bot prototype reduced time spent deciding on nits by ~12 minutes / review
- Hardest cases were correctness comments that lacked a repro; require a repro or explicit owner statement to avoid back-and-forth

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Add a checkbox for "requires canary" in PR template; if ticked add revocation policy and rollout steps
- Add a tiny LLM prompt used by a bot: "Classify the intent of this comment (blocker/correctness/nit/perf/security/docs). Return single token."
- Capture frequent comment pairs (comment + author reply) to build a short FAQ for reviewers

Notes to self: keep this a working doc; iterate fast. Share with Priya + Maya before proposing team-wide changes.
